# Data Source: stripe_quote

A proposal of prices to a customer.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_quote" "onboarding" {
  id = stripe_quote.onboarding.id
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the quote to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `amount_subtotal` - Total before any discounts or taxes are applied.
* `amount_total` - Total after discounts and taxes are applied.
* `application` - ID of the Connect Application that created the quote.
* `application_fee_amount` - The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. There cannot be any line items with recurring prices when using this field.
* `application_fee_percent` - A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice total that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. There must be at least 1 line item with a recurring price to use this field.
* `automatic_tax` - Settings for automatic tax lookup for this quote and resulting invoices and subscriptions. See [`automatic_tax`](#automatic_tax) below.
* `collection_method` - Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay invoices at the end of the subscription cycle or at invoice finalization using the default payment method attached to the subscription or customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as `active`. Defaults to `charge_automatically`. Possible values: `charge_automatically`, `send_invoice`.
* `computed` - See [`computed`](#computed) below.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `customer` - The customer for which this quote belongs to. A customer is required before finalizing the quote. Once specified, it cannot be changed.
* `customer_account` - The account for which this quote belongs to. A customer or account is required before finalizing the quote. Once specified, it cannot be changed.
* `default_tax_rates` - The tax rates that will apply to any line item that does not have `tax_rates` set.
* `description` - A description that will be displayed on the quote PDF. If no value is passed, the default description configured in your [quote template settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/billing/quote) will be used.
* `expires_at` - A future timestamp on which the quote will be canceled if in `open` or `draft` status. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. If no value is passed, the default expiration date configured in your [quote template settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/billing/quote) will be used.
* `footer` - A footer that will be displayed on the quote PDF. If no value is passed, the default footer configured in your [quote template settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/billing/quote) will be used.
* `from_quote` - Clone an existing quote. The new quote will be created in `status=draft`. When using this parameter, you cannot specify any other parameters except for `expires_at`. See [`from_quote`](#from_quote) below.
* `header` - A header that will be displayed on the quote PDF. If no value is passed, the default header configured in your [quote template settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/billing/quote) will be used.
* `invoice` - The invoice that was created from this quote.
* `invoice_settings` - All invoices will be billed using the specified settings. See [`invoice_settings`](#invoice_settings) below.
* `line_items` - A list of line items the customer is being quoted for. Each line item includes information about the product, the quantity, and the resulting cost. See [`line_items`](#line_items) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `number` - A unique number that identifies this particular quote. This number is assigned once the quote is [finalized](https://docs.stripe.com/quotes/overview#finalize).
* `on_behalf_of` - The account on behalf of which to charge.
* `status` - The status of the quote. Possible values: `accepted`, `canceled`, `draft`, `open`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`status_transitions`](#status_transitions) below.
* `subscription` - The subscription that was created or updated from this quote.
* `subscription_data` - When creating a subscription or subscription schedule, the specified configuration data will be used. There must be at least one line item with a recurring price for a subscription or subscription schedule to be created. A subscription schedule is created if `subscription_data[effective_date]` is present and in the future, otherwise a subscription is created. See [`subscription_data`](#subscription_data) below.
* `subscription_schedule` - The subscription schedule that was created or updated from this quote.
* `test_clock` - ID of the test clock to attach to the quote.
* `total_details` - See [`total_details`](#total_details) below.
* `transfer_data` - The data with which to automatically create a Transfer for each of the invoices. See [`transfer_data`](#transfer_data) below.

<a id="automatic_tax"></a>
### `automatic_tax`

The `automatic_tax` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - Automatically calculate taxes
* `liability` - The account that's liable for tax. If set, the business address and tax registrations required to perform the tax calculation are loaded from this account. The tax transaction is returned in the report of the connected account. See [`automatic_tax.liability`](#automatic_tax.liability) below.
* `provider` - The tax provider powering automatic tax.
* `status` - The status of the most recent automated tax calculation for this quote. Possible values: `complete`, `failed`, `requires_location_inputs`.

<a id="automatic_tax.liability"></a>
### `automatic_tax.liability`

The `automatic_tax.liability` attribute supports:

* `account` - The connected account being referenced when `type` is `account`.
* `type` - Type of the account referenced. Possible values: `account`, `self`.

<a id="computed"></a>
### `computed`

The `computed` attribute supports:

* `recurring` - The definitive totals and line items the customer will be charged on a recurring basis. Takes into account the line items with recurring prices and discounts with `duration=forever` coupons only. Defaults to `null` if no inputted line items with recurring prices. See [`computed.recurring`](#computed.recurring) below.
* `upfront` - See [`computed.upfront`](#computed.upfront) below.

<a id="computed.recurring"></a>
### `computed.recurring`

The `computed.recurring` attribute supports:

* `amount_subtotal` - Total before any discounts or taxes are applied.
* `amount_total` - Total after discounts and taxes are applied.
* `interval` - The frequency at which a subscription is billed. One of `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`. Possible values: `day`, `month`, `week`, `year`.
* `interval_count` - The number of intervals (specified in the `interval` attribute) between subscription billings. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` bills every 3 months.
* `total_details` - See [`computed.recurring.total_details`](#computed.recurring.total_details) below.

<a id="computed.recurring.total_details"></a>
### `computed.recurring.total_details`

The `computed.recurring.total_details` attribute supports:

* `amount_discount` - This is the sum of all the discounts.
* `amount_shipping` - This is the sum of all the shipping amounts.
* `amount_tax` - This is the sum of all the tax amounts.
* `breakdown` - See [`computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown`](#computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown) below.

<a id="computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown"></a>
### `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown`

The `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown` attribute supports:

* `discounts` - The aggregated discounts. See [`computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts`](#computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts) below.
* `taxes` - The aggregated tax amounts by rate. See [`computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.taxes`](#computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.taxes) below.

<a id="computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts"></a>
### `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts`

The `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount discounted.
* `discount` - A discount represents the actual application of a [coupon](https://docs.stripe.com/api#coupons) or [promotion code](https://docs.stripe.com/api#promotion_codes). It contains information about when the discount began, when it will end, and what it is applied to. Related guide: [Applying discounts to subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/discounts) See [`computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount`](#computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount) below.

<a id="computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount"></a>
### `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount`

The `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount` attribute supports:

* `checkout_session` - The Checkout session that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular session in payment mode. Not present for subscription mode.
* `customer` - The ID of the customer associated with this discount.
* `customer_account` - The ID of the account representing the customer associated with this discount.
* `end` - If the coupon has a duration of `repeating`, the date that this discount will end. If the coupon has a duration of `once` or `forever`, this attribute will be null.
* `id` - The ID of the discount object. Discounts can't be fetched by ID. Use `expand[]=discounts` in API calls to expand discount IDs in an array.
* `invoice` - The invoice that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice.
* `invoice_item` - The invoice item `id` (or invoice line item `id` for invoice line items of type='subscription') that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice item or invoice line item.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `discount`.
* `promotion_code` - The promotion code applied to create this discount.
* `source` - See [`computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source`](#computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source) below.
* `start` - Date that the coupon was applied.
* `subscription` - The subscription that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription.
* `subscription_item` - The subscription item that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription item.

<a id="computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source"></a>
### `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source`

The `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source` attribute supports:

* `coupon` - The coupon that was redeemed to create this discount.
* `type` - The source type of the discount. Possible values: `coupon`.

<a id="computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.taxes"></a>
### `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.taxes`

The `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.taxes` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount of tax applied for this rate.
* `rate` - Tax rates can be applied to [invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/taxes/tax-rates), [subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) and [Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/use-manual-tax-rates) to collect tax. Related guide: [Tax rates](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) See [`computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate`](#computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate) below.
* `taxability_reason` - The reasoning behind this tax, for example, if the product is tax exempt. The possible values for this field may be extended as new tax rules are supported. Possible values: `customer_exempt`, `not_collecting`, `not_subject_to_tax`, `not_supported`, `portion_product_exempt`, `portion_reduced_rated`, `portion_standard_rated`, `product_exempt`, `product_exempt_holiday`, `proportionally_rated`, `reduced_rated`, `reverse_charge`, `standard_rated`, `taxable_basis_reduced`, `zero_rated`.
* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).

<a id="computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate"></a>
### `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate`

The `computed.recurring.total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate` attribute holds a tax rate, with the attributes of the [`stripe_tax_rate`](../data-sources/tax_rate) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

<a id="computed.upfront"></a>
### `computed.upfront`

The `computed.upfront` attribute supports:

* `amount_subtotal` - Total before any discounts or taxes are applied.
* `amount_total` - Total after discounts and taxes are applied.
* `line_items` - The line items that will appear on the next invoice after this quote is accepted. This does not include pending invoice items that exist on the customer but may still be included in the next invoice. See [`computed.upfront.line_items`](#computed.upfront.line_items) below.
* `total_details` - See [`computed.upfront.total_details`](#computed.upfront.total_details) below.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items"></a>

* `has_more` - True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`. Possible values: `list`.
* `url` - The URL where this list can be accessed.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount_discount` - Total discount amount applied. If no discounts were applied, defaults to 0.

* `amount_total` - Total after discounts and taxes.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. Defaults to product name.
* `discounts` - The discounts applied to the line item. See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.discounts`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.discounts) below.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `item`.
* `price` - The price used to generate the line item. See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.price`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.price) below.
* `quantity` - The quantity of products being purchased.
* `taxes` - The taxes applied to the line item. See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes) below.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data.price"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price` attribute supports:

* `active` - Whether the price can be used for new purchases.
* `billing_scheme` - Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `unit_amount` or `unit_amount_decimal`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for prices with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for prices with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes. Possible values: `per_unit`, `tiered`.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `currency_options` - Prices defined in each available currency option. Each key must be a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) and a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options) below.
* `custom_unit_amount` - When set, provides configuration for the amount to be adjusted by the customer during Checkout Sessions and Payment Links. See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.custom_unit_amount`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.custom_unit_amount) below.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `lookup_key` - A lookup key used to retrieve prices dynamically from a static string. This may be up to 200 characters.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `nickname` - A brief description of the price, hidden from customers.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `price`.
* `product` - The ID of the product this price is associated with.
* `recurring` - The recurring components of a price such as `interval` and `usage_type`. See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.recurring`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.recurring) below.
* `tax_behavior` - Only required if a [default tax behavior](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/products-prices-tax-categories-tax-behavior#setting-a-default-tax-behavior-(recommended)) was not provided in the Stripe Tax settings. Specifies whether the price is considered inclusive of taxes or exclusive of taxes. One of `inclusive`, `exclusive`, or `unspecified`. Once specified as either `inclusive` or `exclusive`, it cannot be changed. Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`, `unspecified`.
* `tiers` - Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`. See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.tiers`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.tiers) below.
* `tiers_mode` - Defines if the tiering price should be `graduated` or `volume` based. In `volume`-based tiering, the maximum quantity within a period determines the per unit price. In `graduated` tiering, pricing can change as the quantity grows. Possible values: `graduated`, `volume`.
* `transform_quantity` - Apply a transformation to the reported usage or set quantity before computing the amount billed. Cannot be combined with `tiers`. See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.transform_quantity`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.transform_quantity) below.
* `type` - One of `one_time` or `recurring` depending on whether the price is for a one-time purchase or a recurring (subscription) purchase. Possible values: `one_time`, `recurring`.
* `unit_amount` - The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a whole integer if possible. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.

### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options` attribute is a map. Each value supports:

* `custom_unit_amount` - When set, provides configuration for the amount to be adjusted by the customer during Checkout Sessions and Payment Links. See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options.custom_unit_amount`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options.custom_unit_amount) below.
* `tax_behavior` - Only required if a [default tax behavior](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/products-prices-tax-categories-tax-behavior#setting-a-default-tax-behavior-(recommended)) was not provided in the Stripe Tax settings. Specifies whether the price is considered inclusive of taxes or exclusive of taxes. One of `inclusive`, `exclusive`, or `unspecified`. Once specified as either `inclusive` or `exclusive`, it cannot be changed. Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`, `unspecified`.
* `tiers` - Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`. See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options.tiers`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options.tiers) below.
* `unit_amount` - The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a whole integer if possible. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options.custom_unit_amount"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options.custom_unit_amount`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options.custom_unit_amount` attribute supports:

* `maximum` - The maximum unit amount the customer can specify for this item.
* `minimum` - The minimum unit amount the customer can specify for this item. Must be at least the minimum charge amount.
* `preset` - The starting unit amount which can be updated by the customer.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options.tiers"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options.tiers`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.currency_options.tiers` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `flat_amount` - Price for the entire tier.
* `flat_amount_decimal` - Same as `flat_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.
* `unit_amount` - Per unit price for units relevant to the tier.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - Same as `unit_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.
* `up_to` - Up to and including to this quantity will be contained in the tier.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.custom_unit_amount"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.custom_unit_amount`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.custom_unit_amount` attribute supports:

* `maximum` - The maximum unit amount the customer can specify for this item.
* `minimum` - The minimum unit amount the customer can specify for this item. Must be at least the minimum charge amount.
* `preset` - The starting unit amount which can be updated by the customer.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.recurring"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.recurring`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.recurring` attribute supports:

* `interval` - The frequency at which a subscription is billed. One of `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`. Possible values: `day`, `month`, `week`, `year`.
* `interval_count` - The number of intervals (specified in the `interval` attribute) between subscription billings. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` bills every 3 months.
* `meter` - The meter tracking the usage of a metered price
* `usage_type` - Configures how the quantity per period should be determined. Can be either `metered` or `licensed`. `licensed` automatically bills the `quantity` set when adding it to a subscription. `metered` aggregates the total usage based on usage records. Defaults to `licensed`. Possible values: `licensed`, `metered`.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.tiers"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.tiers`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.tiers` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `flat_amount` - Price for the entire tier.
* `flat_amount_decimal` - Same as `flat_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.
* `unit_amount` - Per unit price for units relevant to the tier.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - Same as `unit_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.
* `up_to` - Up to and including to this quantity will be contained in the tier.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.transform_quantity"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.transform_quantity`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.price.transform_quantity` attribute supports:

* `divide_by` - Divide usage by this number.
* `round` - After division, either round the result `up` or `down`. Possible values: `down`, `up`.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount of tax applied for this rate.
* `rate` - Tax rates can be applied to [invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/taxes/tax-rates), [subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) and [Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/use-manual-tax-rates) to collect tax. Related guide: [Tax rates](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes.rate`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes.rate) below.
* `taxability_reason` - The reasoning behind this tax, for example, if the product is tax exempt. The possible values for this field may be extended as new tax rules are supported. Possible values: `customer_exempt`, `not_collecting`, `not_subject_to_tax`, `not_supported`, `portion_product_exempt`, `portion_reduced_rated`, `portion_standard_rated`, `product_exempt`, `product_exempt_holiday`, `proportionally_rated`, `reduced_rated`, `reverse_charge`, `standard_rated`, `taxable_basis_reduced`, `zero_rated`.
* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes.rate"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes.rate`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes.rate` attribute supports:

* `active` - Defaults to `true`. When set to `false`, this tax rate cannot be used with new applications or Checkout Sessions, but will still work for subscriptions and invoices that already have it set.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the tax rate for your internal use only. It will not be visible to your customers.
* `display_name` - The display name of the tax rates as it will appear to your customer on their receipt email, PDF, and the hosted invoice page.
* `effective_percentage` - Actual/effective tax rate percentage out of 100. For tax calculations with automatic_tax[enabled]=true, this percentage reflects the rate actually used to calculate tax based on the product's taxability and whether the user is registered to collect taxes in the corresponding jurisdiction.
* `flat_amount` - The amount of the tax rate when the `rate_type` is `flat_amount`. Tax rates with `rate_type` `percentage` can vary based on the transaction, resulting in this field being `null`. This field exposes the amount and currency of the flat tax rate. See [`computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes.rate.flat_amount`](#computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes.rate.flat_amount) below.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `inclusive` - This specifies if the tax rate is inclusive or exclusive.
* `jurisdiction` - The jurisdiction for the tax rate. You can use this label field for tax reporting purposes. It also appears on your customer’s invoice.
* `jurisdiction_level` - The level of the jurisdiction that imposes this tax rate. Will be `null` for manually defined tax rates. Possible values: `city`, `country`, `county`, `district`, `multiple`, `state`.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `tax_rate`.
* `percentage` - Tax rate percentage out of 100. For tax calculations with automatic_tax[enabled]=true, this percentage includes the statutory tax rate of non-taxable jurisdictions.
* `rate_type` - Indicates the type of tax rate applied to the taxable amount. This value can be `null` when no tax applies to the location. This field is only present for TaxRates created by Stripe Tax. Possible values: `flat_amount`, `percentage`.
* `state` - [ISO 3166-2 subdivision code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2), without country prefix. For example, "NY" for New York, United States.
* `tax_type` - The high-level tax type, such as `vat` or `sales_tax`. Possible values: `amusement_tax`, `communications_tax`, `digital_excise_tax`, `gst`, `hst`, `igst`, `jct`, `lease_tax`, `mass_transit_parking_tax`, `parking_tax`, `pst`, `qst`, `retail_delivery_fee`, `rst`, `sales_tax`, `service_tax`, `utility_users_tax`, `vat`.

<a id="computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes.rate.flat_amount"></a>
### `computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes.rate.flat_amount`

The `computed.upfront.line_items.data.taxes.rate.flat_amount` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount of the tax when the `rate_type` is `flat_amount`. This positive integer represents how much to charge in the smallest currency unit (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).
* `currency` - Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase.

<a id="computed.upfront.total_details"></a>
### `computed.upfront.total_details`

The `computed.upfront.total_details` attribute supports:

* `amount_discount` - This is the sum of all the discounts.
* `amount_shipping` - This is the sum of all the shipping amounts.
* `amount_tax` - This is the sum of all the tax amounts.
* `breakdown` - See [`computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown`](#computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown) below.

<a id="computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown"></a>
### `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown`

The `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown` attribute supports:

* `discounts` - The aggregated discounts. See [`computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts`](#computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts) below.
* `taxes` - The aggregated tax amounts by rate. See [`computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.taxes`](#computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.taxes) below.

<a id="computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts"></a>
### `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts`

The `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount discounted.
* `discount` - A discount represents the actual application of a [coupon](https://docs.stripe.com/api#coupons) or [promotion code](https://docs.stripe.com/api#promotion_codes). It contains information about when the discount began, when it will end, and what it is applied to. Related guide: [Applying discounts to subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/discounts) See [`computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount`](#computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount) below.

<a id="computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount"></a>
### `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount`

The `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount` attribute supports:

* `checkout_session` - The Checkout session that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular session in payment mode. Not present for subscription mode.
* `customer` - The ID of the customer associated with this discount.
* `customer_account` - The ID of the account representing the customer associated with this discount.
* `end` - If the coupon has a duration of `repeating`, the date that this discount will end. If the coupon has a duration of `once` or `forever`, this attribute will be null.
* `id` - The ID of the discount object. Discounts can't be fetched by ID. Use `expand[]=discounts` in API calls to expand discount IDs in an array.
* `invoice` - The invoice that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice.
* `invoice_item` - The invoice item `id` (or invoice line item `id` for invoice line items of type='subscription') that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice item or invoice line item.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `discount`.
* `promotion_code` - The promotion code applied to create this discount.
* `source` - See [`computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source`](#computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source) below.
* `start` - Date that the coupon was applied.
* `subscription` - The subscription that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription.
* `subscription_item` - The subscription item that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription item.

<a id="computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source"></a>
### `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source`

The `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source` attribute supports:

* `coupon` - The coupon that was redeemed to create this discount.
* `type` - The source type of the discount. Possible values: `coupon`.

<a id="computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.taxes"></a>
### `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.taxes`

The `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.taxes` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount of tax applied for this rate.
* `rate` - Tax rates can be applied to [invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/taxes/tax-rates), [subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) and [Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/use-manual-tax-rates) to collect tax. Related guide: [Tax rates](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) See [`computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate`](#computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate) below.
* `taxability_reason` - The reasoning behind this tax, for example, if the product is tax exempt. The possible values for this field may be extended as new tax rules are supported. Possible values: `customer_exempt`, `not_collecting`, `not_subject_to_tax`, `not_supported`, `portion_product_exempt`, `portion_reduced_rated`, `portion_standard_rated`, `product_exempt`, `product_exempt_holiday`, `proportionally_rated`, `reduced_rated`, `reverse_charge`, `standard_rated`, `taxable_basis_reduced`, `zero_rated`.
* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).

<a id="computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate"></a>
### `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate`

The `computed.upfront.total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate` attribute holds a tax rate, with the attributes of the [`stripe_tax_rate`](../data-sources/tax_rate) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

<a id="from_quote"></a>
### `from_quote`

The `from_quote` attribute supports:

* `is_revision` - Whether this quote is a revision of a different quote.
* `quote` - The quote that was cloned.

<a id="invoice_settings"></a>
### `invoice_settings`

The `invoice_settings` attribute supports:

* `custom_fields` - A list of up to 4 custom fields to be displayed on the invoice. See [`invoice_settings.custom_fields`](#invoice_settings.custom_fields) below.
* `days_until_due` - Number of days within which a customer must pay invoices generated by this quote. This value will be `null` for quotes where `collection_method=charge_automatically`.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `footer` - Footer to be displayed on the invoice.
* `issuer` - See [`invoice_settings.issuer`](#invoice_settings.issuer) below.

<a id="invoice_settings.custom_fields"></a>
### `invoice_settings.custom_fields`

The `invoice_settings.custom_fields` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `name` - The name of the custom field.
* `value` - The value of the custom field.

<a id="invoice_settings.issuer"></a>
### `invoice_settings.issuer`

The `invoice_settings.issuer` attribute supports:

* `account` - The connected account being referenced when `type` is `account`.
* `type` - Type of the account referenced. Possible values: `account`, `self`.

<a id="line_items"></a>
### `line_items`

The `line_items` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `adjustable_quantity` - See [`line_items.adjustable_quantity`](#line_items.adjustable_quantity) below.
* `amount_discount` - Total discount amount applied. If no discounts were applied, defaults to 0.
* `amount_subtotal` - Total before any discounts or taxes are applied.
* `amount_tax` - Total tax amount applied. If no tax was applied, defaults to 0.
* `amount_total` - Total after discounts and taxes.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. Defaults to product name.
* `discounts` - The discounts applied to the line item. See [`line_items.discounts`](#line_items.discounts) below.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `item`.
* `price` - The price used to generate the line item.
* `price_data` - See [`line_items.price_data`](#line_items.price_data) below.
* `quantity` - The quantity of products being purchased.
* `tax_rates` -
* `taxes` - The taxes applied to the line item. See [`line_items.taxes`](#line_items.taxes) below.

<a id="status_transitions"></a>
### `status_transitions`

The `status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `accepted_at` - The time that the quote was accepted. Measured in seconds since Unix epoch.
* `canceled_at` - The time that the quote was canceled. Measured in seconds since Unix epoch.
* `finalized_at` - The time that the quote was finalized. Measured in seconds since Unix epoch.

<a id="subscription_data"></a>
### `subscription_data`

The `subscription_data` attribute supports:

* `billing_mode` - The billing mode of the quote. See [`subscription_data.billing_mode`](#subscription_data.billing_mode) below.
* `description` - The subscription's description, meant to be displayable to the customer. Use this field to optionally store an explanation of the subscription for rendering in Stripe surfaces and certain local payment methods UIs.
* `effective_date` - When creating a new subscription, the date of which the subscription schedule will start after the quote is accepted. This date is ignored if it is in the past when the quote is accepted. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that will set metadata on the subscription or subscription schedule when the quote is accepted. If a recurring price is included in `line_items`, this field will be passed to the resulting subscription's `metadata` field. If `subscription_data.effective_date` is used, this field will be passed to the resulting subscription schedule's `phases.metadata` field. Unlike object-level metadata, this field is declarative. Updates will clear prior values.
* `trial_period_days` - Integer representing the number of trial period days before the customer is charged for the first time.

<a id="subscription_data.billing_mode"></a>
### `subscription_data.billing_mode`

The `subscription_data.billing_mode` attribute supports:

* `flexible` - See [`subscription_data.billing_mode.flexible`](#subscription_data.billing_mode.flexible) below.
* `type` - Controls how prorations and invoices for subscriptions are calculated and orchestrated. Possible values: `classic`, `flexible`.

<a id="subscription_data.billing_mode.flexible"></a>
### `subscription_data.billing_mode.flexible`

The `subscription_data.billing_mode.flexible` attribute supports:

* `proration_discounts` - Controls how invoices and invoice items display proration amounts and discount amounts. Possible values: `included`, `itemized`.

### `total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount`

* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `discount`.
* `promotion_code` - The promotion code applied to create this discount.
* `source` - See [`total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source`](#total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source) below.
* `start` - Date that the coupon was applied.
* `subscription` - The subscription that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription.
* `subscription_item` - The subscription item that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription item.

<a id="total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source"></a>
### `total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source`

The `total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source` attribute supports:

* `coupon` - The coupon that was redeemed to create this discount.
* `type` - The source type of the discount. Possible values: `coupon`.

<a id="total_details.breakdown.taxes"></a>
### `total_details.breakdown.taxes`

The `total_details.breakdown.taxes` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount of tax applied for this rate.
* `rate` - Tax rates can be applied to [invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/taxes/tax-rates), [subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) and [Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/use-manual-tax-rates) to collect tax. Related guide: [Tax rates](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) See [`total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate`](#total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate) below.
* `taxability_reason` - The reasoning behind this tax, for example, if the product is tax exempt. The possible values for this field may be extended as new tax rules are supported. Possible values: `customer_exempt`, `not_collecting`, `not_subject_to_tax`, `not_supported`, `portion_product_exempt`, `portion_reduced_rated`, `portion_standard_rated`, `product_exempt`, `product_exempt_holiday`, `proportionally_rated`, `reduced_rated`, `reverse_charge`, `standard_rated`, `taxable_basis_reduced`, `zero_rated`.
* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).

<a id="total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate"></a>
### `total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate`

The `total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate` attribute holds a tax rate, with the attributes of the [`stripe_tax_rate`](../data-sources/tax_rate) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

<a id="transfer_data"></a>
### `transfer_data`

The `transfer_data` attribute supports:

* `amount` - The amount in cents (or local equivalent) that will be transferred to the destination account when the invoice is paid. By default, the entire amount is transferred to the destination.
* `amount_percent` - A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice total that will be transferred to the destination account. By default, the entire amount will be transferred to the destination.
* `destination` - The account where funds from the payment will be transferred to upon payment success.
